t: No provision which is included in the appropriations Act enumerated in section 101 but which was not included in the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 1995 and which by its terms is applicable to more than one appropriation, fund, or authority shall be applicable to any appropriation, fund, or authority provided in this joint resolution.

fable.w: This is a continuing-resolution provision limiting the applicability of general provisions from enumerated appropriations Acts to funds provided in the joint resolution. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government; there is no tempting reading beyond the generic word "authority", which refers to budget authority.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical provision regarding the scope and applicability of specific clauses within an appropriations bill. It defines which provisions apply to which funds or authorities. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: No provision which is included in the appropriations Act enumerated in section 101 but which was not included in the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 1995 and which by its terms is applicable to more than one appropriation, fund, or authority shall be applicable to any appropriation, fund, or authority provided in this joint resolution.

opus.w: This section only says which provisions of the enumerated appropriations Acts apply to the funding in this joint resolution. It describes no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue that involves anyone outside the federal government. The reference to appropriations Acts is technical funding language, not a process for outsiders to take part in a decision.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The only possible pull toward "Yes" is that the section talks about appropriations Acts, which Congress passes, so it sounds procedural. That reading fails. This is standard continuing-resolution wording that limits which provisions carry over to the funding in this joint resolution. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, given a comment period, or given a right to sue. No rulemaking is authorized either. This matches Example 1, which was also a funding provision.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical provision limiting the applicability of certain clauses in an appropriations act. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. It merely defines which statutory provisions apply to specific funds, involving no external participation.
qwen_chat.s: No provision which is included in the appropriations Act enumerated in section 101 but which was not included in the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 1995 and which by its terms is applicable to more than one appropriation, fund, or authority shall be applicable to any appropriation, fund, or authority provided in this joint resolution.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references "appropriations Acts" and "authorities," it implies a legislative process involving public input. However, the text itself is purely a technical limitation on the applicability of certain provisions within a joint resolution. It does not describe any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from any party outside the federal government (including Congress, which is inside the government). It is a rule of statutory construction, not a participation mechanism.
